title: Text to Speech with ElevenLabs
summary: Generate audio through a server API client while preserving bytes, credentials, and response types.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Ultimate Guide to Using Eleven Labs API: Transform Text to Lifelike Speech in Minutes!

richText: Send text and receive audio
Text to speech converts text into an audio recording. Use it for a user-requested reading of an article or journal entry.
ElevenLabs exposes POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}. The request body contains text and can select a supported model_id. The response is audio bytes.
The example requests mp3_44100_128 and uses eleven_multilingual_v2. Check the current provider documentation for available voices, models, formats, permissions, and account limits.
POST is appropriate because generation performs an action and may consume paid quota. Do not make a GET endpoint automatically generate new audio.
These examples use Spring Boot 3.2+, Spring Framework 6.1+, and Java 17. Configure the same connect and read timeouts explained on External GET and POST APIs.
Keep the API key on the server
Set elevenlabs.api-key from ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in environment configuration. Inject that property into the server client. Never send the key to browser code.
Supply a voice ID the application allows. Read available IDs from the provider rather than treating any user string as a remote URL.
The snippet belongs in a configuration class. Its JDK request factory sets connection and read timeouts.
Preserve binary data and its media type
Use byte[] instead of String. Decoding MP3 bytes as text damages the recording.
The provider Content-Type tells the browser which audio format it received. Preserve that value when sending the bytes from your own controller.
A successful result contains audio bytes and an audio Content-Type. The browser can play those bytes through an audio element or save them as a file.
Bound requests and explain failures
Validate nonblank text and an application text-length limit before contacting the provider. For long recordings, use streaming or a background job instead of buffering the whole response.
Handle provider authentication errors, rate limits, and timeouts as failures. A JSON error body must never be returned as an MP3.
Ask for an explicit generation action before sending private journal text to an external service. Avoid logging the text or audio.
A retry after a timeout can generate and charge twice. Use the provider duplicate-prevention contract if one exists. Do not assume that ordinary HTTP retries are safe.
